evidence.quote: requiring OAuth 2.0-based user, bot, or workspace tokens
Lists all users in a Slack team.
Gets the access logs for the current team.

assumptions: The source gives no rate limit details, so none are set.

Slack's error codes (ratelimited, invalid_auth, not_authed, token_revoked, account_inactive) and the 'ok'/'error' response fields are from general Slack knowledge, not this document; the 'ok' field does appear in responses.

The user list has no per-user last-active field, so login history (team.accessLogs) is used as the activity signal. It needs the 'admin' scope and, as far as I know, a paid Slack plan; the source does not state the plan.
Access logs give one record per user, device and IP with the last login time, and Slack may limit how far back they go. The source does not say.
The cursor parameter on users.list and the page/count parameters on team.accessLogs are documented, but maximum page sizes are not. 200 and 100 are my choices.
Slack tokens can also be sent as a Bearer header, but the source only shows a 'token' query parameter, so that is what the API key method uses.
Users with 'deleted' true are mapped to deleted. Slack's users.list normally includes deactivated users, but the source does not say so.
Role is based only on the is_admin flag. Owners and guests are not separately distinguished.
Pagination for users.list uses response_metadata.next_cursor, taken from the sample response.

The team.accessLogs call lists 'token' as a required query parameter. It is included with an empty placeholder value, and I am assuming the runtime fills in the real token from the chosen sign-in method.
